Code of practice.

(2) The power of the Minister under subsection (1){a) or {b) to issue or approve as a code of practice shall include the power to issue or approve a part of such a code of practice or document.

(3) a code of practice is issued, approved, amended or revoked by the Minister under subsection ( 1), the Minister shall - {a) publish a notice of such issue, approval, amendment or revocation, as the case may be, in such manner as will secure adequate publicity for such issue, approval, amendment or revocation; {b) specify in the notice referred to in paragraph {a) the date of issue, amendment or revocation, as the case may be; {c) ensure that, so long as the code of practice remains in force, copies of that code, and of all amendments to that code, are available -

(6) Any code of practice shall be deemed not to be subsidiary legislation. Use of codes of practice in criminal proceedings.

(1) A person shall not be liable to any criminal proceedings by reason only that he has failed to observe any code of practice.

(2) In any proceedings for any offence against this Order, a code of practice that is relevant to any matter which it is necessary for the prosecution to prove in to establish the commission of the offence shall be admissible in evidence in the proceedings.

(3) Without affecting any other method of proof, in any proceedings for an offence against this Order {a) the production of a document purporting to be a copy of a notice published by the Minister under section 74(3){a) shall be taken to be such a notice until the contrary is proved; and {b) the production of a code of practice, or an amendment or a revocation of a code of practice, purporting to be the subject of a notice section 74(3){a} shall be taken to be the subject of that notice until the contrary is proved.

Unless the context otherwise requires, any offence under this Order may be tried by a Court of a Magistrate or a Syariah Subordinate Court, as the case may be, and such Court shall, notwithstanding the provisions of the Criminal Procedure Code (Chapter 7) and any other written law, have jurisdiction to impose the maximum penalty provided for by this Order.
The Lunacy Act is repealed. Construction of other written laws.

(a) to a lunatic or mental person shall be construed as a reference to a mentally disordered person; 9th. TUNE, 2014

(b) to lunacy shall be construed as a reference to mental disorder;

(c) to an asylum, a lunatic asylum, a mental hospital, a mental facility or any other medical facility for the purpose of admitting, remanding, confining or detaining a mentally disordered person shall be construed as a reference to a psychiatric facility. Amendment of Chapter 51.

Section 7 of the Old Age and Disability Pensions Act is amended by deleting paragraph (d) and by substituting the following new paragraph therefor - "(d) allowances for a mentally disordered person who is under the provisions of the Mental Health Order, 2014, either detained in a psychiatric facility or committed to the care of any relative or friend, or his dependants;". Amendment of Old Age and Disability Pensions Regulations in Chapter 18.

(a) any order made under that Act and in force immediately prior to the commencement of this Order shall, so far as it is not inconsistent with the provisions of this Order, continue to be in force and have effect as if it had been made under this Order until it is amended or repealed;

(b) any inquiry or proceedings commenced under that Act prior to the of this Order shall be continued or concluded under and in with the corresponding provisions of this Order.
